decision: Keep Paitan Lake and Vaca Dam Reservoir as separate inland-water leads. Do not turn a joint stocking announcement, historical aggregate surveys, or conflicting news reports into current wild-presence or catchability claims.

sources.title: CLSU-CF, DA-BFAR and LGU initiate stock enhancement of Paitan Lake and Vaca Dam Reservoir
sourceReportedScope: Vaca Dam Reservoir, Llanera, Nueva Ecija
allocationAndIdentityLimits: The article describes one joint activity and does not allocate any count or fish group between the two waterbodies.
Only Nile tilapia is a specific common-name label; the source gives no scientific names. 'Mudfish' and 'carp' are broad common-name groups and are not silently resolved to taxa.
Stocking documents an introduction event, not survival, reproduction, current presence, wild status, abundance or a catch record.
sources.reuse: The official page was reviewed for minimal event facts. No item-specific reuse license was identified; no page image or prose is copied.
sources.disposition: Stocking-event evidence only; zero wild-occurrence or app assertions.

sources.title: Survey of Endemic, Indigenous and Introduced (Foreign) Species in the Freshwater Ecosystems of Nueva Ecija
sources.sourceReportedMethod: Three stations were selected in each study area, with ten randomly laid 10 m by 12 m quadrats per station. The abstract says fish, mollusks and macroflora were collected; it does not provide sampling dates or a species-by-waterbody table.
sources.reuse: No item-specific license or reuse grant was identified in the reviewed official PDF.
sources.disposition: Historical survey-scope lead for Paitan and Pantabangan; aggregate counts cannot be allocated to an individual lake or treated as a complete checklist.

sources.title: Endemic, Indigenous, and Introduced Species in the Freshwater Ecosystems of Nueva Ecija and Pampanga: Status, Diversity, and Impacts
sourceReportedScope: Five Nueva Ecija waters including Paitan Lake and Pantabangan Dam
Pampanga Main River areas at Apalit, San Simon and San Luis
sources.access: The official metadata/indexed abstract was reviewed. The journal PDF endpoint returned HTTP 404 during this review; no full article table was transcribed.
sources.authorRelationship: Three authors overlap with the 2006 NAST freshwater survey, and both sources cover five Nueva Ecija waters. Do not count their related historical richness totals as independent estimates.
sources.reuse: The Silliman Journal policy reviewed for this project states journal/author co-ownership and requires written permission to reproduce an article in full or two or more tables/figures. No item-specific open license was identified.
sources.disposition: Historical source lead only; no species-by-waterbody row is admitted from the inaccessible table.

sources.title: Ecija execs deny presence of janitor fish in huge lake
sources.sourceType: news report quoting local officials and a DENR statement
conflictingStatements: The article quotes Cuyapo's mayor saying a DENR team checked the reported janitor fish and found none.
Later in the same article, the report attributes to DENR a statement identifying Pterygoplichthys pardalis in Paitan Lake.
sources.qualityAndTimeLimits: The report does not provide a survey method, date or voucher and contains internally conflicting presence statements. The alleged finding is from 2009 and cannot establish current presence.
sources.disposition: Conflict lead only; do not admit Pterygoplichthys pardalis or any other species from this article.

legacyLocalityQueries.decision: Invalid for biological coverage conclusions because GBIF marks taxon key 204 for Actinopterygii deleted on 2022-11-23. The six saved exact-text zeroes are invalidated and are not evidence of fish absence. Do not claim corrected locality searches were run in this batch.

currentTaxonSelection.scope: Actinopterygii only; a ray-finned-fish search does not cover sharks or rays.

scopeLimits: The joint stocking count is not split between Paitan and Vaca Dam.
No validated waterbody polygon, sampling station, reach, salinity class, or legal fishing boundary was obtained.
The historical studies do not provide an accessible, rights-cleared, verified species-by-waterbody table in this review.
No source here establishes current abundance, catchability, food safety, fishing permission, or absence of a species.
nextStep: Continue the Central Luzon freshwater and wetland source sweep using corrected CoL XR fish filters once the GBIF query window is stable; in parallel, inventory Paitan, Vaca Dam, Candaba and the Pampanga basin from accessible official/primary sources. Keep stocking, survey and catch evidence distinct, and leave Central Luzon incomplete.
